title: Lincoln Center film, the Olympics tour and a James Brown extra show
summary: Lincoln Center plans a film of the dancers, some members leave with the Olympics tour, and the troupe does an extra show with a Tonight Show shot.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So, now all of this is happening to get to these tap dancers, you see. So Lincoln Center -- they called. The Lincoln Center Library -- they finally called. And there was some star photographer, John Stones, he wanted to -- he was employed by, I think, the Lincoln Center Library to make a

story, to take a film of these tap dancers.
Now, this is during the time of the Olympics. One of the members -- in fact -- yeah -- one of the members and a future member was committed to perform on this tour with the Olympics, you see. They had to go to Japan, Africa, I think, Mexico and so forth -- Spain -- somewhere in there, you know. And then they come back to America.

By that time we had to move out of there, see. Now, from performing in the Apollo Theater, we had to pinch hit, do an extra show for Mr. James Brown, you know. What they call him? He sang so he had to have these -- this great -- some kind of music. He was doing studious music, I call it, because -- poor boy made good, other words, right?

So, it was the Tonight -- the Johnny Carson -- the Tonight Show. They said that we was to do that extra show anyhow in the (unintelligible) House, and they would give us a shot on the Tonight Show. They said they couldn't employ the whole amount, but some of them tap dance.

So, we wanted the buck to be the buck, so we accepted. And then it's all beginning to happen, and it's starting out. So, there we come. We got this chance to go down and get orchestrations, and new costumes, and to premier, you know, and then be contracted, you see. And in a way it was, of course -- I think they was going to enlarge it -- this house, see. See, but the tap dancers are being -- they're being

commercialized, you know. Like Sandman got called away on a tour and -- which he always is called away. And the other one, the Good Father, Boston Jimmy Sly, he never could do the Sundays, you know. He had to go back to Massachusetts. And that's where his home is. He had to do his Sundays up there.

That's how I started to call them the on-the-town dancers these names, you see. Good Father and -- well, they liked it see. At least -- because the audience -- it was entertaining to the audience, you see.
